capacity.value: 1 litre of working solution per 135 roll at 1+4

reuse.value: One-shot at 1+4. DD-X is Ilford's speed-increasing developer and gives roughly +1 stop over ID-11.

capacity.value: 1 litre of working solution at 1+4 develops about 4 rolls one-shot

reuse.value: One-shot at 1+4. Stock can be reused with time compensation, but Kodak's published tables are for one-shot use.

capacity.value: One-shot at every dilution; a 500 ml bottle makes dozens of rolls

reuse.value: Never reused. Fomadon R09 is Foma's Rodinal-equivalent: a para-aminophenol developer that keeps for years and gives sharp, grainy, compensating negatives.

capacity.value: One-shot at every dilution; 500 ml makes around 50 rolls at 1+25

reuse.value: Never reused. Adonal is Adox's Rodinal equivalent, with the same long shelf life and compensating behaviour.

capacity.value: Per Adox's instructions; one bottle makes 500 ml of working solution

reuse.value: One-shot. A special low-contrast developer made for CMS 20 II; it is the only developer that gives the microfilm emulsion a printable contrast.

capacity.value: 1 litre of working solution: about 8 rolls, or more with the supplied replenishment routine

reuse.value: A two-bath C-41 kit at 38 °C, sold as a powder or liquid set. Developer is one-shot; bleach and fix can be reused.

capacity.value: 1 litre: about 8 rolls, with a published capacity table

reuse.value: A monobath: developer, stop and fix in one solution, used once per session and then discarded. Convenient, but it fixes contrast and grain to one look.

crossProcess.summary: Velvia 100 through C-41: the same cross-process family as Velvia 50, with a slightly higher contrast and a stronger magenta cast.
crossProcess.colourShifts: Cyan-green shadows, magenta midtones and yellow highlights. Skin goes distinctly red.
crossProcess.contrastChange: Very high, with both ends steepened and a usable latitude of about a stop.
crossProcess.grainChange: Fine and slightly tighter than the film in E-6.
crossProcess.exposureNotes: Rate at EI 50–80 and meter for the highlights.
crossProcess.expectedResult: A dense, saturated negative with a strong colour cast, best scanned.
crossProcess.limitations: The look cannot be neutralised without losing the contrast that justifies the process. Times vary between kits.
examples: A common cross-processing stock since Velvia 100 replaced Velvia 50 in many kits.

crossProcess.summary: Provia 100F in C-41 gives a cooler, softer cross-process than Velvia: less saturation, gentler contrast, and a blue-cyan cast.
crossProcess.colourShifts: Blue-cyan shadows and green-yellow midtones, with a gentler cast than Velvia.
crossProcess.contrastChange: High, but less extreme than Velvia in the same process.
crossProcess.exposureNotes: Rate at EI 64–100 and expose for the shadows, which go empty quickly.
crossProcess.expectedResult: A cool, contrasty negative that scans with a strong cyan cast.
crossProcess.limitations: The cast is less dramatic than Velvia's, which for many photographers defeats the purpose.
examples: Used by photographers who want a cross-process look without Velvia's saturation.

crossProcess.summary: Portra 160 in E-6: a pale, low-contrast transparency with a green-cyan cast and soft colour.
crossProcess.colourShifts: Green-cyan overall, with pale shadows and slightly yellow highlights.
crossProcess.contrastChange: Lower than the film's normal C-41 contrast.
crossProcess.grainChange: Fine; barely changed by the process.
crossProcess.exposureNotes: Overexpose by one stop against box speed; the transparency is very thin at box speed.
crossProcess.expectedResult: A pale, soft transparency with a green cast.
crossProcess.limitations: The orange mask is not removed, so the colour balance cannot be corrected in the chemistry.
examples: A common 'slide from negative stock' experiment.

crossProcess.summary: Portra 800 in E-6 is thin and grainy, with the contrast compressed and the shadows empty. It is a test rather than a process.
crossProcess.colourShifts: Strong green-cyan cast with muddy highlights.
crossProcess.grainChange: Coarser and more visible than in C-41.
crossProcess.exposureNotes: Overexpose by one to two stops and expect little shadow detail.
crossProcess.expectedResult: A pale, grainy transparency with a heavy cast.
crossProcess.limitations: No reliable published times; results vary widely between E-6 kits.

crossProcess.summary: CineStill has already had its rem-jet removed. Running it through an ECN-2 pre-bath gains nothing and the alkaline bath can damage the emulsion.
crossProcess.colourShifts: None to gain: the stock is a cinema emulsion already.
crossProcess.contrastChange: Unpredictable, and generally thinner than a C-41 development.
crossProcess.grainChange: Unchanged in principle, but the pre-bath can reticulate the emulsion.
crossProcess.exposureNotes: No usable exposure index for this route.
crossProcess.expectedResult: At best an ordinary negative with a damaged emulsion; at worst a ruined roll.
crossProcess.limitations: The rem-jet is gone, so the reason for ECN-2 has gone with it. Develop CineStill in C-41.

crossProcess.summary: Vision3 500T in C-41 after a proper rem-jet pre-bath: this is exactly what CineStill 800T is, and it works.
crossProcess.colourShifts: A slight blue-cyan cast from the ECN-2 to C-41 gamma difference, correctable in the scan.
crossProcess.contrastChange: A little higher than ECN-2, because C-41 is a still-film process.
crossProcess.grainChange: Fine, and slightly more visible than in ECN-2.
crossProcess.exposureNotes: Rate at EI 500–800 depending on the look wanted.
crossProcess.expectedResult: A clean, low-contrast colour negative with strong latitude.
crossProcess.limitations: Only after the rem-jet pre-bath. Without it the backing survives, mottles and contaminates the chemistry.
examples: CineStill 800T and several other respools are exactly this process.

crossProcess.summary: Fomapan 100 through C-41: dense, contrasty and heavily stained, like other B&W cross-processes but with a distinctly Foma warmth.
crossProcess.colourShifts: Warm brown base and yellow highlights, with muddy shadows.
crossProcess.contrastChange: Much higher than a normal B&W development.
crossProcess.exposureNotes: Rate at EI 50–80; C-41 develops the film far beyond its normal contrast.
crossProcess.expectedResult: A thick, stained negative that scans better than it prints.
crossProcess.limitations: The stain is uneven and the negative is harder to print than to scan.
examples: A cheap way into cross-processing for anyone with a C-41 kit and a roll of Foma.
